doc.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Meeting again in Nagasaki on the drum-battle tour
summary: They met again on George Wein's Japan tour with Blakey, Tony Williams, Wayne Shorter and McCoy.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: So you met him again, four years later, how did that happen?

Well when we went to Japan on one of George Wein’s tours. This was supposed to be like the drum battle so it was Art Blakey, Tony Williams and myself. Oh yeah Wayne Shorter, Ben Tucker. Who was playing piano? I forgot. McCoy! Yeah, and the next time her father sponsored one of the…when we went to Nagasaki he was one of the sponsors.
When, Keiko, when you were first in the country and you were with your father, what was your father’s job? Keiko Jones: My father, long story but short he wants to sell the public… (Inaudible)
So you were in the states in 1962 and then you went back to Japan? And when did you get back from Japan, cause you meet Elvin in ’66?
We were staying in the America for the only six days. New York for two days because I wanted to hear the jazz but I missed the opportunity.
(Laughs) That’s a very aggressive drummer in that situation.
So you met again in Nagasaki? So you went to Nagasaki to perform during this drum battle tour?
